# dsh-chat-preset
A DeepSeek Harness bundle that registers a `chat` agent preset: a plain helpful assistant with web a
ccess and local skills, and no way to touch the filesystem or run a command.
## Abstract
The harness composes behaviour from bundles, presets, and plugins. This bundle adds one preset row a
nd one guard plugin, so a session can be switched to a chat mode whose model can search, fetch, and
load skill instructions, and nothing else. A preset-scope tool restriction would also filter the pre
set's own tools, so the restriction is applied per agent once that agent exists.
## What it registers
One preset, mounted from `cordis.patch.yml`:
| Field | Value |

| `id` | `chat` |
| `name` | Chat |
| `order` | 5 |
| persona | helpful assistant, cites sources, ma

rks uncertainty, never claims to have run something it did not |
| tools | `web_search`, `web_fetch`

, `skill` |
| compaction | basic compaction plus `/compact` |
The persona is `complete: true`, so it replaces rather than extends the host prompt, and `includeRun
timeContext` is off: chat mode does not get the workspace facts injected.
## Why a guard instead of a config flag
The preset's own tools are registered in the shared preset scope, and the host also registers a few
global tools such as `working_directory`. A restriction applied at the preset scope would filter the
preset's own tools too, and would miss the globals. So the restriction is applied per agent, once t
ols too, and would miss the globals. So the restriction is applied per agent, once the agent exists.
`lib/guard.js` listens for `agent/created`, reads the tools that agent can actually see, keeps `web_
search` and `web_fetch`, adds `skill` when it is present, and calls `agent.ctx.tools.restrict({ allo
` and `web_fetch`, adds `skill` when it is present, and calls `agent.ctx.tools.restrict({ allow })`.
Reading the allow list from the visible tools rather than hard-coding it means a search-only or fetc
h-only web configuration still produces the right restriction instead of an empty one. If no web too
l is registered at all, the guard logs a warning and leaves the inherited tools unrestricted, which
is a deliberate failure mode: it prefers a visible configuration error over silently removing a tool
the user asked for.
## Why the skill tool survives
`skill` reads only the skill files that the discovery provider exposes. It never resolves a workspac
e path, so keeping it does not widen filesystem access. Dropping it would make user-level skills unr
eachable in the one mode that most needs them.

## Verification
| Check | Command | Result |

| Unit tests | `node --test test/guard.test.mjs` | pass, 6 tests |
| Module parses | `node --check l

ib/guard.js` | pass |
| Install layout | clone into a temporary `DSH_HOME`, then check the package a
nd its patch arrive | pass; `pnpm install` and a harness restart were not run |
**Not tested:** a full preset switch in a freshly installed harness. The machine this bundle was wri
tten on runs the preset, but no separate live check was repeated from this repository.
## Limitations
- The guard restricts tools, not prompts. A chat session can still load any skill the discovery prov

ider exposes, by design.
- The preset rows name shipped harness packages (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-pr
eset`, `dsh-persona`, `dsh-agent-instructions`, and the skill and compaction plugins). They are reso
lved from the harness install and are not vendored here.
## References
1. DeepSeek Harness. <https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness>. MIT.
